title: The CEO Who Let His Own Factory Burn for Insurance
hook: A factory fire kills three workers, but the CEO smiles—he already bet against his own building.
why_this_can_go_viral: Moral outrage + hidden scheme = massive shareability. Viewers will ask 'how did he get away with it?'

title: The Hedge Fund That Paid Hackers to Delay a Rival's Trades
hook: Milliseconds decide billions—so one fund paid criminals to slow down their competitors' servers.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reveals a secret war in finance most people don't know exists. High 'insider info' vibe.

title: The Startup That Raised $50M by Faking a User Base of 10 Million
hook: They built a dashboard that showed '10M users'—it was just a spreadsheet and 10 people clicking.
why_this_can_go_viral: Perfect mix of 'greedy founders' and 'stupid VCs.' The reveal is explosive and relatable to startup culture.

title: The Spy Who Faked a Job at a Rival's Waste Management to Steal Trade Secrets
hook: Nobody guards the trash—so a corporate spy became a janitor and pulled billions from the dumpster.
why_this_can_go_viral: Classic 'low-tech attack on high-tech' story. Easy to visualize, easy to retell.

title: The Ad That Used Hidden Subliminal Sounds to Make You Buy More
hook: You didn't decide to buy that drink—a 1-second audio clip buried in the ad decided for you.
why_this_can_go_viral: Paranoia trigger + real science controversy = endless discussion in comments.

title: The Factory That Mixed Sawdust Into Baby Formula to Cut Costs
hook: Parents fed their babies 'nutrition'—it was mostly wood. And it was legal for years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Baby harm instantly evokes emotion. The 'legal for years' detail fuels outrage and sharing.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Organic' Food—It Was Just Regular Produce With Fake Labels
hook: Organic certification is a sticker. One startup bought a label printer and tripled their profit overnight.
why_this_can_go_viral: Hits the wellness crowd hard. Everyone who pays premium for organic will share in disbelief.

title: The Monopoly That Bought Every Radio Station and Played Only Its Own Music
hook: You never heard the better song—because one company owned the airwaves and silenced competition.
why_this_can_go_viral: Music lovers and creators unite against a common enemy. 'Imagine never hearing your favorite artist.'

title: The Spy Who Stole a Rival's Formula by Tattooing It on His Back
hook: He couldn't take notes past security—so he memorized the formula and inked it onto his skin.
why_this_can_go_viral: Bizarre, visual, and almost unbelievable. The 'tattoo secret' hook is highly shareable.

title: The Ad Campaign That Gave You Discounts—in Exchange for Your DNA
hook: A free coupon costs you your privacy—but one company wanted more: your genetic code.
why_this_can_go_viral: Privacy fears + biotechnology = perfect storm. Viewers will debate 'would you trade DNA for a deal?'

title: The Factory That Recycled Hospital Waste Into Cheap Toys
hook: Your child's plastic dinosaur was once a used syringe. And the label said 'safe for all ages.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme disgust + child safety = unstoppable virality. Parents will share immediately.

title: The Startup That Paid Fake Users to Post Rave Reviews—and Destroyed Competitors
hook: They hired 1,000 people to write glowing reviews. Their rivals? The same people wrote 1-star reviews.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone has seen suspicious reviews. This confirms the darkest suspicion—and goes viral on that trust.

title: The Monopoly That Made Landlords Use Its 'Mandatory' App to Pay Rent
hook: They owned the property and the software. Rent had to go through their app—and they skimmed 3%.
why_this_can_go_viral: Renters and housing advocates share instantly. 'You're forced to use their app to pay them?' is infuriating.

title: The Spy Who Posed as a Photographer to Shoot a Rival's Secret Prototype
hook: They hired a photographer for a 'press event'—he was really shooting their next product from every angle.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visual and clever. 'How to steal a billion-dollar product with a camera' is a great story to share.

title: The Ad That Targeted You Based on Your Voice—Without You Saying a Word
hook: Your phone wasn't listening—but the billboard was. It adjusted the ad based on your facial expression.
why_this_can_go_viral: Creepy tech that feels like Black Mirror. Viewers will share to warn others about surveillance.

title: The Industry That Hid the Fact That Its 'Safe' Chemical Causes Infertility
hook: For decades, they knew the chemical in your plastic bottle could make you sterile. They sold it anyway.
why_this_can_go_viral: Personal health threat + corporate betrayal = explosive virality. Everyone wants to know if they're affected.

title: The Trader Who Used a Seismic Sensor to Predict Factory Output
hook: He didn't need earnings reports—he just listened to the ground shake when the machines ran.
why_this_can_go_viral: Genius low-tech hack in a high-tech world. 'How to beat Wall Street with a rock' is a great hook.

title: The Startup That Faked a Government Contract to Raise Its Valuation
hook: They photoshopped a letter from the Department of Defense. Investors wired $30 million the next week.
why_this_can_go_viral: Shows how little due diligence happens. 'They believed a PDF?' is both funny and terrifying.

title: The Monopoly That Kept Generic Drugs Off the Market by Paying Rivals $1B
hook: They didn't lower prices—they paid competitors billions to not compete. You paid 10x for your pills.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone buys medicine. The 'pay for delay' scheme is infuriating and highly shareable.
